package_info.package_versions: All versions of affected Magento e-commerce sites
package_info.why_malicious: The injected JavaScript code is designed to steal payment information from customers by capturing credit card data entered on checkout pages and exfiltrating it to attacker-controlled servers. This constitutes credential theft and data exfiltration, which is highly malicious and illegal.

execution_context.trigger: When a user submits the checkout form during the payment process
execution_context.file_location: Injected into Magento e-commerce site JavaScript files, typically within checkout page scripts (e.g., app/design/frontend/*/template/checkout/*.phtml or pub/static/frontend/*/en_US/js/checkout.js)
required_permissions: Access to the DOM to read form input fields
Permission to initiate outbound network requests (fetch/XHR)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user submits the checkout form, the code attaches an event listener to the form submission, reads credit card data directly from the DOM input fields, and sends the collected data via an HTTPS POST request to an attacker-controlled external domain, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive payment information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code intercepts sensitive credit card data at the point of form submission and transmits it to an external, untrusted domain, which is a hallmark of client-side skimming attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate checkout scripts should only transmit payment data to trusted payment processors or gateways, never to unknown or unverified external domains. Directly accessing and exfiltrating raw credit card data from the DOM is not expected in secure e-commerce implementations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate scripts may access payment fields for client-side validation or to pass data to secure payment APIs, but they do not send raw card data to domains outside of authorized payment processors.
key_indicators: Event listener attached to checkout form submission
Direct access to credit card input fields (number, expiry, cvv) in the DOM
Outbound HTTPS POST request to a domain not associated with the merchant or payment processor
No user notification or consent for data transmission to external server

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects malicious JavaScript into the Magento site's checkout page scripts.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is loaded and executed in the browser of users visiting the checkout page.

attack_chain.action: The malicious JavaScript attaches an event listener to the checkout form and captures credit card data as users submit payment information.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive payment data (card number, expiry, CVV) is harvested from the user's browser.

attack_chain.action: The captured credit card data is exfiltrated to an attacker-controlled server via an HTTPS POST request.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment information, enabling potential financial fraud.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code attaching event listeners to checkout or payment form submissions
Client-side scripts reading credit card fields (number, expiry, cvv) directly from the DOM
Outbound network requests (fetch/XHR) from checkout pages to domains not associated with legitimate payment processors
file_indicators: Unexpected or recently modified JavaScript files in Magento theme, template, or static asset directories (e.g., app/design/frontend/*/template/checkout/*.phtml, pub/static/frontend/*/en_US/js/checkout.js)
Inline scripts on checkout pages referencing or sending data to unknown external domains
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests from client browsers on checkout pages to domains not belonging to the merchant or known payment processors (e.g., attacker-domain.com/collect)
Unusual or new outbound traffic patterns from checkout pages to external IPs or domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Regularly scan all JavaScript files and inline scripts on checkout pages for code that accesses credit card input fields and initiates outbound requests to untrusted domains. Monitor network logs for POST requests from checkout pages to unknown external domains. Use web application firewalls to block or alert on outbound requests to domains not on an allowlist of trusted payment processors. Implement file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized changes to checkout-related scripts.
